page.text:
Both the continuity of $f$ and the connectedness of the interval $[a, b]$
are indispensable to the Intermediate Value Theorem.

A function with a jump discontinuity can skip directly from negative to
positive values without attaining zero. Similarly, if the domain is
disconnected (such as $[0, 1] \cup [2, 3]$), a continuous function may
take negative values on the first component and positive values on the
second without ever crossing zero. Topologically, the theorem states that
the continuous image of a connected space is connected, and the connected
subsets of $\mathbb{R}$ are precisely intervals.
